implementation: Actual case service now implements decision-v1 DeliverWorkflowReceipt and ReconcileWorkflowReceipt. Existing case mutation rules, execution-wide body binding and full attempt/redrive receipts share one owner transaction and the existing receipt table. Duplicate attempts retain the original case; different bodies conflict.

Added opt-in integration-token HTTP receipt routes, bounded strict decoding and tenant authorization. RouterConfig.EnableWorkflowReceipts defaults to false and no command/deployment configuration enables it.

Added decision workflowreceipt HTTP adapter with a fixed case-service destination, explicit credential/timeout, HTTPS by default, no redirects, bounded strict response validation and echoed receipt identity. Legacy HTTP success and HTTP errors never establish receipt acceptance.

Added a public integration-test fixture that installs the real participating PostgreSQL owner definitions in generated disposable databases. The actual decision client was exercised against the actual case router/service/repositories with a committed action followed by an intentionally lost HTTP response; reconciliation recovered its case without resending.
Repaired selected existing workflow test fixtures to install the real identity owner schema needed by case contributor reads. No production behavior was bypassed to obtain passing tests.

verification.scope: New owner/HTTP receipt cases plus existing workflow grouping, idempotency, metadata validation and rollback regressions. New cases cover eight concurrent duplicates, lost-response lookup, new attempts, conflicting bodies, authority and identity rejection, and final receipt insertion failure rolling back case/link/audit writes.
Strict client wire protocol, destination/redirect policy and actual PostgreSQL case-owner lost-response reconciliation.

remaining_requirements: D19.17 remains open: this implements the real PostgreSQL case-action provider. It does not implement the staged MySQL case mutation owner or external add_tag/emit_event receipt receivers.
D19.19 and D19.20 still need intended scoring/outbox provider contracts and destination/receipt semantics. Repository searches found these explicitly unresolved, not existing complete receiver APIs.
D14.12 and D15.17 still require user-agreed numeric targets. Existing repository throughput measurements are historical observations explicitly disclaimed as approved SLOs.
Shared MySQL all-provider composition, trusted runtime worker identities, restricted grants, crash/uncertain-commit lifecycle acceptance and sustained load remain open.
limitations: No checklist leaves were newly ticked; 152/152 has not been achieved.

The source-owner fixtures seed authoritative decisions and use explicit setup authority. The actual HTTP receiver verifies its configured service token and tenant allowlist; this is not D19.21 trusted-worker or D20 full runtime certification.
Lost HTTP response is covered; injected process death and uncertain database commit acknowledgement remain separate gates.
Only generated disposable databases in decision-cycle11 were used. No application reset, deployment, runtime activation or separate per-service application database was introduced.
